package.name: ingest
package.packageFile:
# INGEST, migrating one node at a time.
#
# Abyssale is the first. The other three are still TypeScript and each is blocked on something
# different, which is worth writing down because the package name suggests otherwise — "ingest REST
# nodes" was on the backlog as ready, and reading them proved it wrong:
#
#   PlaidTransactions  MIGRATED 2026-07-28 needing NO new capability, which is not what this note said a
#                      day earlier. All three of its supposed blockers dissolved once the vendor API was
#                      read rather than the old code.
#   GoogleSheet        MIGRATED as a REWRITE: it was a Sheets client AND a loop in one node, holding rows
#                      in actor state. It returns every row now and LoopStart/LoopEnd iterate.
#   DocumentParser     RETIRED and REPLACED by unstructured/ParseDocument. It parsed pdf/docx in process
#                      with `pdf-parse` and `mammoth`, which no manifest can express — and did not need
#                      to, once one HTTP call covered the same job and twenty more formats.
#   Document           RETIRED with no replacement: it existed to feed DocumentParser, and every metadata
#                      field it emitted came from its own input.
#   SpatialIngest      MIGRATED 2026-07-28 by DELETING the pipeline rather than describing it. It had
#                      reimplemented the content engine — 373 lines, 220 of them a drifted COPY of the
#                      engine's extraction prompts and schemas, with its own embedding call and its own
#                      write to the dictionary. The engine's MANUAL connector was written for this node
#                      and never used. Now it hands raw text over and the engine does the rest.

name: ingest
displayName: Ingest
description: Content ingestion, template rendering and data import
version: 2.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Render branded images and PDFs from Abyssale templates
  - Fetch realistic test bank transactions from Plaid Sandbox
  - Read rows from a public Google Sheet

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): SpatialIngest hands its
  # text to the platform's own content engine over `scope.engineUrl` (127.0.0.1:4101), same
  # declaration the spatial package carries for its searches.
  - 127.0.0.1
  - api.abyssale.com
  # Plaid picks its host from the credential's environment, so all three are declared. A sandbox key
  # cannot reach production and vice versa, so listing them is not a widening.
  - sheets.googleapis.com
  - sandbox.plaid.com
  - development.plaid.com
  - production.plaid.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"
  # apiKeyHeader for Abyssale (x-api-key), apiKeyQuery for Google Sheets (?key=). Plaid needs
  # neither: it authenticates in the request BODY, so it declares no scheme at all.
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  # Abyssale generation is asynchronous: POST to start, then ask the generation request until it is
  # finalized. Without `poll` the node would settle on the RECEIPT — a request id — and emit that as
  # the finished asset, with nothing reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.abyssaleCredential.yaml:
name: abyssaleCredential
displayName: Abyssale
description: Abyssale API credentials for high-quality template rendering

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Abyssale API key from the dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Abyssale API key
credentials.googleApiCredential.yaml:
# MOVED HERE, not copied, and moved NOW even though GoogleSheet is still TypeScript.
#
# Credential declaration is all-or-nothing per package: `registerCredentialType` is
# first-wins-and-SILENT, so a credentials/*.yaml alongside a live `api.registerCredential()` means
# whichever loads first takes the slot and the other vanishes — surfacing later as an auth failure
# with the right credential visibly selected. Migrating ONE node therefore moves EVERY credential the
# package declares.
#
# Nothing breaks for the code nodes: the type registry is shared, so GoogleSheet reads
# `googleApiCredential` exactly as before. Only the source of the declaration changed.

name: googleApiCredential
displayName: Google API
description: Google API credentials for accessing Google services

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Google API key with Sheets API enabled
    placeholder: Enter your Google API key
credentials.plaidCredential.yaml:
# Moved with the others — see googleApiCredential.yaml for why declaration is all-or-nothing.

name: plaidCredential
displayName: Plaid
description: Plaid API credentials for accessing banking data (Sandbox/Development/Production)

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Plaid client ID from the Plaid Dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid client ID
  - name: secret
    displayName: Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Plaid secret key (use Sandbox secret for testing)
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid secret
  - name: environment
    displayName: Environment
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: "Plaid environment: sandbox, development, or production"
    placeholder: sandbox
    default: sandbox

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE GET. This is the whole of talking to Google Sheets — the code version's 186-line executor was
# iteration bookkeeping, not API work.
#
# `apiKeyQuery`, because Sheets takes the key as `?key=`, not a header. That scheme already existed.
#
# THE RANGE IS ENCODED. A1 notation contains `!` and often a sheet name with spaces, and it sits in the
# PATH — unencoded, "My Sheet!A1:D10" produces a malformed URL that 400s with a message about the
# range rather than about the encoding. `encodeURIComponent` is in the sandbox for exactly this.

- name: values
  method: GET
  url: "return 'https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/' + config.spreadsheetId + '/values/' + encodeURIComponent(config.range || 'Sheet1')"

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyQuery
    param: key
    value: "{{ credentials.googleApiCredential.apiKey }}"

  query:
    # The code version's own two: rows rather than columns, and raw values rather than the
    # display-formatted strings, so a number arrives as a number.
    majorDimension: ROWS
    valueRenderOption: UNFORMATTED_VALUE

  transport: json

  # Google answers with { error: { code, message, status } }. The message is already specific — "Unable
  # to parse range", "The caller does not have permission" — so it is surfaced as-is rather than
  # replaced by a guess, with one addition: a 403 on this endpoint almost always means the sheet is not
  # shared, which the vendor's wording does not say and the reader needs to hear.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: |
      return (() => {
        const e = response.error;
        const hint = e.code === 403
          ? ' — check the sheet is shared so anyone with the link can view it, and that the API key has the Sheets API enabled'
          : '';
        return e.message + hint;
      })();
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [spreadsheetId]
  properties:
    spreadsheetId:
      type: string
      title: Spreadsheet ID
      description: >-
        The id from the sheet's URL — the part between /d/ and /edit. The sheet must be shared so that
        anyone with the link can view it; an API key cannot open a private sheet.
      placeholder: Enter your Google Sheets spreadsheet ID
    range:
      type: string
      title: Range
      description: A1 notation range, e.g. Sheet1!A1:D10. A bare sheet name reads the whole sheet.
      placeholder: Sheet1!A:Z
      default: Sheet1
    useHeaders:
      type: boolean
      title: Use Headers
      description: Treat the first row as property names, so each row arrives as an object
      default: true
"ui:order": [spreadsheetId, range, useHeaders]
files.interface.yaml:
# THIS NODE'S SHAPE CHANGED, and it is the one migration here that is a REWRITE rather than a
# transcription. Stated plainly because a saved workflow will notice.
#
# The code version was a CallbackNode that held the fetched rows in ACTOR STATE and emitted ONE ROW per
# `continue` signal, tracking its own position. So it was two things at once: a Google Sheets client and
# a loop. Its outputs were `item`, `index`, `total`, `hasMore`.
#
# The platform now has the loop as its own pair of nodes. `LoopStart` and `LoopEnd` iterate anything,
# keeping their index in Redis rather than in an actor, so this node no longer has to — and doing it
# here meant every row-by-row workflow depended on a private actor nobody else could reuse.
#
# So it returns EVERY ROW, once, and iteration is wired: GoogleSheet → LoopStart → … → LoopEnd.
#
# `item`, `index` and `hasMore` are GONE. A workflow that wired them was driving the actor and has to
# be rewired around LoopStart; there is no way to keep those names honest without keeping the actor.
# `total` is kept, unchanged, because it still means exactly what it did.

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Nothing is read from it — the sheet is named in config.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: >-
      Every row in the range. Objects keyed by the header row when Use Headers is on, otherwise raw
      arrays of cell values.
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: Number of rows returned

credentials:
  - name: googleApiCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
type: GoogleSheet
# A PromiseNode now, where the code version was a CallbackNode. That is the whole of this migration:
# see interface.yaml for what changed on the wire and why.
kind: PromiseNode

name: Google Sheet
category: Storage & Data
color: "#34A853"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1753618586/gravity/icons/googleSheetIcon.png

description: Read rows from a public Google Sheets spreadsheet

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to read rows from a public GOOGLE SHEET. It returns every row in one go, so pair it with Loop
  Start and Loop End when each row needs to flow through its own workflow steps. It reads a Google
  Sheet specifically, not an app-owned database table.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A sheet is edited by people, so the same request legitimately answers differently an hour later.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# Running this live needs INGEST_GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) and a spreadsheet id of your own,
# SHARED so anyone with the link can view it — an API key cannot open a private sheet, which is the
# failure the error message above exists to explain.
#
# The id below is a placeholder rather than a real sheet: inventing one that happened to resolve would
# make this fixture pass for a reason nobody chose.

testData:
  config:
    spreadsheetId: 1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTuVwXyZ0123456789ABCDEFG
    range: Sheet1!A1:D10
    useHeaders: true
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # AN ARRAY OF OBJECTS, not merely an array. With useHeaders on, getting raw arrays back means the
    # header branch was skipped — which is exactly what happens if the sheet has only one row, so this
    # distinguishes "mapped correctly" from "fell through".
    rows: >-
      return Array.isArray(output.rows)
        && output.rows.length > 0
        && typeof output.rows[0] === 'object'
        && !Array.isArray(output.rows[0])
    # The count must AGREE with what came out. A total read off the wrong array would still be a
    # plausible number.
    total: "return output.total === output.rows.length"
